exportSetup.title: Export settings
exportSetup.containerHint: File format of the result. mp4 plays anywhere, mkv holds almost any combination of streams, mov is the usual choice for further editing.
exportSetup.videoCodecHint: libx264 encodes quickly and plays on any device. libx265 makes the file about a third smaller at the same quality, but encodes several times slower and is not supported everywhere.
exportSetup.qualityHint: Constant quality factor: the lower the number, the better the picture and the larger the file. 18 is visually lossless, 23 is the ffmpeg default, above 28 the artefacts become visible.
exportSetup.presetHint: Trade between encoding time and file size. Slower presets take longer and pack the same quality into fewer bytes; the picture quality itself is set by CRF.
exportSetup.resolutionHint: Frame size of the result. Every clip is scaled to fit it, the aspect ratio is kept and the remaining space is filled with black bars.
exportSetup.frameRateHint: Frames per second in the result. All clips are converted to this rate; a rate above the source one adds no smoothness, it only enlarges the file.
exportSetup.speedHint: Playback speed of the result. 1 keeps the original pace, values above it shorten the video, values below it stretch it. The sound follows the picture and keeps its pitch.
exportSetup.audioCodecHint: Encoder for the sound track. aac is the standard companion of mp4 and plays everywhere, libmp3lame is the classic mp3, ac3 is used by DVD and broadcast.
exportSetup.audioBitrateHint: Sound quality: 128 is enough for speech, 192 is the usual choice for music, above 256 the difference is barely audible.
